cues.en: Why are gas stations always built right next to other gas stations?
cues.zh: 为什么加油站总是建在别的加油站旁边？

cues.en: Why is it that I can drive for a mile without finding a coffee shop and then stumble across three on the same corner? Why do grocery stores, auto repair shops, and restaurants always seem to exist in groups instead of being spread evenly throughout a community.
cues.zh: 为什么我开了一英里都找不到一家咖啡店，然后却在同一个街角偶然发现三家？为什么杂货店、汽车修理店和餐馆似乎总是扎堆出现，而不是均匀分布在整个社区里。

cues.en: While there are several factors that might go into deciding where to place your business, clusters of similar companies can be explained by a very simple story called Hotelling's Model of Spatial Competition.
cues.zh: 虽然决定企业选址可能涉及多个因素，但相似公司的聚集可以用一个非常简单的理论来解释，叫做霍特林空间竞争模型。

cues.en: Imagine that you sell ice cream at the beach. Your beach is one mile long and you have no competition.
cues.zh: 想象你在海滩上卖冰淇淋。你的海滩有一英里长，而且没有竞争对手。

cues.en: Where would you place your cart in order to sell the most product? In the middle. The one half mile walk may be too far for some people at each end of the beach, but your cart serves as many people as possible.
cues.zh: 你会把推车放在哪里才能卖出最多产品？放在中间。对海滩两端的一些人来说，半英里的路程可能太远了，但你的推车能服务尽可能多的人。

cues.en: One day you show up at work just as your cousin Teddy is arriving at the beach with his own ice cream cart. In fact, he's selling exactly the same type of ice cream as you are.
cues.zh: 有一天你来上班，正好你表弟Teddy带着他自己的冰淇淋推车来到海滩。事实上，他卖的冰淇淋和你完全一样。

cues.en: You agree that you will split the beach in half. In order to ensure that customers don't have to walk too far, you set up your cart a quarter mile south of the beach center, right in the middle of your territory.
cues.zh: 你同意把海滩一分为二。为了确保顾客不用走太远，你把餐车放在海滩中心以南四分之一英里处，正好在你地盘的正中间。

cues.en: Teddy sets up a quarter mile north of the center in the middle of Teddy territory.
cues.zh: Teddy 把餐车放在中心以北四分之一英里处，正好在 Teddy 地盘的正中间。

cues.en: With this agreement, everyone south of you buys ice cream from you. Everyone north of Teddy buys from him, and the 50% of beachgoers in between walk to the closest cart.
cues.zh: 按照这个协议，你南边的所有人都会找你买冰淇淋，Teddy 北边的所有人都会找他买，而中间那 50% 的海滩游客会走向离自己更近的餐车。

cues.en: No one walks more than a quarter of a mile, and both vendors sell to half of the beachgoers.
cues.zh: 没人会走超过四分之一英里的路，而且两个小贩都能卖给一半的海滩游客。

cues.en: Game theorists consider this a socially optimal solution.
cues.zh: 博弈论学者认为这是社会最优解。

cues.en: It minimizes the maximum number of steps any visitor must take in order to reach an ice cream cart.
cues.zh: 它能让任何游客走到冰淇淋车所需的最大步数最小化。

cues.en: The next day when you arrive at work, Teddy has set up his cart in the middle of the beach.
cues.zh: 第二天你上班时，Teddy已经把车摆在了海滩正中间。

cues.en: You return to your location a quarter mile south of center and get the 25% of customers to the south of you. Teddy's still gets all of the customers north in Teddy territory,
cues.zh: 你回到中心以南四分之一英里的位置，拿到了南边25%的顾客。Teddy仍然拿下他地盘北边的所有顾客，

cues.en: but now you split the 25% of people in between the two carts.
cues.zh: 但现在你们俩平分了中间那25%的人。

cues.en: Day three of the ice cream wars, you get to the beach early and set up right in the center of Teddy territory,
cues.zh: 冰淇淋大战第三天，你早早来到海滩，正好扎在Teddy地盘的中央，

cues.en: assuming you'll serve the 75%
cues.zh: 以为能拿下南边75%的

cues.en: of beachgoers to your South, leaving your cousin to sell to the 25% of customers to the North. When Teddy arrives, he sets up just south of you, stealing all of the southerly customers and leaving you with a small group of people to the North.
cues.zh: 海滩游客，让表弟卖给北边25%的顾客。Teddy来了，就在你南边扎营，抢走了所有南边的顾客，只给你留下北边一小撮人。

cues.en: Not to be outdone, you move 10 paces south of Teddy to regain your customers.
cues.zh: 你不想认输，往Teddy南边挪了10步，想抢回顾客。

cues.en: When you take a midday break, Teddy shuffles 10 paces south of you and again steals back all the customers to the far end of the beach. Throughout the course of the day, both of you continue to periodically move south towards the bulk of the ice cream buyers until both of you eventually end up at the center of the beach back to back, each serving 50% of the ice cream hungry beachgoers.
cues.zh: 当你午休时，Teddy向南挪了10步，又把所有顾客都抢回到海滩的另一端。一天下来，你们俩都不断向南移动，靠近购买冰淇淋的主力人群，直到最后你们俩都到了海滩中央，背对背，各自服务50%想吃冰淇淋的沙滩游客。

cues.en: At this point, you and your competitive cousin have reached what game theorists call a Nash equilibrium,
cues.zh: 这时，你和你的竞争对手表亲达到了博弈论所说的纳什均衡，

cues.en: the point where neither of you can improve your position by deviating from your current strategy.
cues.zh: 也就是你们谁都无法通过偏离当前策略来改善自身处境的那个点。

cues.en: Your original strategy, where you were each a quarter mile from the middle of the beach, didn't last because it wasn't a Nash equilibrium.
cues.zh: 你最初各自位于海滩中点四分之一英里处的策略没能维持下去，因为它不是纳什均衡。

cues.en: Either of you could move your cart towards the other to sell more ice cream.
cues.zh: 你们中任何一方都可以把车移向对方，从而卖出更多冰淇淋。

cues.en: With both of you now in the center of the beach, you can't reposition your cart closer to your furthest customers
cues.zh: 现在你们俩都在海滩中央，你无法把车挪到离最远顾客更近的位置

cues.en: without making your current customers worse off. However, you no longer have a socially optimal solution since customers at either end of the beach have to walk further than necessary to get a sweet treat.
cues.zh: 而不损害现有顾客的利益。然而，你不再拥有社会最优解，因为海滩两端的顾客不得不走更远的路才能买到甜点。

cues.en: Think about all the fast food chains, clothing boutiques, or mobile phone kiosks at the mall. Customers may be better served by distributing services throughout a community, but this leaves businesses vulnerable to aggressive competition.
cues.zh: 想想商场里的快餐连锁店、服装精品店或手机摊位。把服务分散到社区各处，顾客可能得到更好的服务，但这让企业容易受到激烈竞争的冲击。

cues.en: In the real world, customers come from more than one direction, and businesses are free to compete with marketing strategies by differentiating their product line and with price cuts. But at the heart of their strategy,
cues.zh: 现实世界中，顾客来自不止一个方向，企业可以自由地通过差异化产品线和降价等营销策略来竞争。但在其战略核心，

cues.en: companies like to keep their competition as close as possible.
cues.zh: 企业喜欢让竞争对手尽量靠近自己。
